chunks.text: DRYER GUIDE How to Use the Dryer Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Never dry anything that has had gasoline, solvents or any oil on it, including cooking oil, even after washing. Fire risk. Items with foam, rubber or plastic: dry them on a clothesline or with Air Dry only.

Clean the lint screen before every load. Do not let children play on or in the dryer, and do not reach in while the drum is moving. Use the dryer only when you are at home. Keep gasoline and other flammable products away from it.

1 Clean the lint screen: pull it straight up, roll the lint off with your fingers and push the screen firmly back in. Do not rinse it. From the manufacturer's manual, 2 Open the door and put the laundry in loosely. Do not overload: clothes must tumble freely. Add one dryer sheet to the wet load if you want (not with steam cycles), then close the door.
3 Load size: small is 3 to 4 items (1/4 full), medium is 1/2 full, large is 3/4 full.

2 Turn the cycle knob. Auto cycles sense when clothes are dry and save energy: Normal or Eco Normal for everyday loads, Heavy Duty for towels and jeans, Casual for shirts and synthetics, Delicate for lingerie and washable woollens, Damp Dry for clothes you want to iron. Timed Dry runs for a set time (up to 100 minutes).

3 If you want, change the settings. Auto cycles: press Dryness Level for More, Normal or Less (set it before you start). Timed Dry: use More Time or Less Time and press Temperature. Use the lowest heat if you are unsure. 4 Foam, rubber, plastic, shower curtains or rubber-backed rugs: use Timed Dry with Air Dry (no heat), or hang them up.

5 Steam models only: Quick Refresh freshens 1 to 9 dry items. Enhanced Touch Up removes wrinkles from a load left in the dryer. Do not add dryer sheets, and wash new or starched clothes first. 6 If you cannot unload as soon as it ends, press Wrinkle Shield: it tumbles the load now and then for up to 90 minutes. 7 Press and hold START/PAUSE to start.

1 The lights show the stage: Sensing, Wet, Damp, Cool Down, Done. At Damp you can take out items you want to hang or iron. 2 To pause, press START/PAUSE once. To cancel, press POWER. 3 To lock the buttons, press and hold Cycle Signal for 3 seconds. Do the same to unlock them.

4 When Done lights up, take the clothes out straight away so they do not wrinkle. Let Cool Down finish first: clothes can be hot. Drying rack (if your dryer has one) 1 For sweaters or shoes that should not tumble: hook the rack into the door opening and rest the back on the rear ledge. Leave the lint screen in. Use Timed Dry or Air Dry only. Clean the lint screen afterwards.

STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT You smell gas: do not touch any switch or phone in the building. Leave, call the gas supplier from outside, then property management. A burning smell or smoke: press POWER and do not use the dryer again. An "F" code (for example F1 E1) shows on the display, or the dryer does not heat.

If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management. Based on the manufacturer's manual W10385092A for this Whirlpool electronic dryer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Never run the dryer with the lint screen loose, damaged, blocked or missing. It can overheat. Keep gasoline and other flammable products away from the dryer. Keep the area around the dryer clear, including piles of laundry in front of it.

1 Clean the lint screen before or after each load. Pull it straight up, roll the lint off with your fingers and push it firmly back in. 2 Use only one dryer sheet per load, and only once. A sheet stuck on the air grille behind the lint screen slows drying. From the manufacturer's manual,

3 If lint falls into the dryer while you take the screen out, tell property management: it can collect in the vent. Every 6 months, or when it looks clogged: wash the lint screen 1 Detergent and softener can coat the screen. It is clogged if lint falls off it while it is in the dryer, or if clothes take longer to dry.

2 Roll the lint off, then wet both sides of the screen with hot water. 3 Scrub the screen with a nylon brush, hot water and liquid detergent to remove build-up. From the manufacturer's 4 Rinse it with hot water, dry it well with a clean towel and put it back.

1 Wipe the drum with a soft cloth and a little mild dish soap in very warm water. Or use a microfiber cloth with hot water from a spray bottle, then dry it with a second cloth. 2 Rinse with a wet sponge or towel, then tumble a load of clean towels to dry it.

3 Blue marks from jeans on the drum are harmless and do not transfer to other clothes. Dry jeans and bright cottons inside out to avoid them. 1 Keep the area around the dryer clear of lint, dust, laundry piles and anything that blocks air flow. 2 Before you go away for a long time, clean the lint screen. Use the dryer only when you are at home.

3 Property management arranges cleaning of the inside of the dryer and the vent at least every 2 years. Do not open the dryer yourself. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT Clothes take much longer than usual to dry, or the display shows "AF": the vent may be blocked.

The lint screen is damaged or missing, or the drum light stops working (it needs a special 10-watt appliance bulb). On steam models, the water hose is bulging, kinked or leaking. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
Based on the manufacturer's manual W10385092A for this Whirlpool electronic dryer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

DRYER GUIDE Dryer Troubleshooting Whirlpool Model (to confirm) Do not open the dryer cabinet or try to repair it. Never dry anything that has had oil, gasoline or solvents on it. 1 Close the door completely. 2 Press and hold START/PAUSE for 2 to 5 seconds. 3 If the Control Lock light is on, press and hold Cycle Signal for 3 seconds to unlock.

4 "PE" on the display means the power went off. Press and hold START/PAUSE to restart. 5 Check the dryer's breakers in the electrical panel (electric dryers use two). If one has tripped and trips again, contact property management. Clothes take too long to dry 2 Dry smaller loads so clothes can tumble freely. 3 Check that Air Dry is not selected (it uses no heat).

4 If an Auto cycle stops too early, choose More with the Dryness Level button. 5 "AF" on the display means low airflow. Clean the lint screen and press any button to clear it. 6 Check no dryer sheet is stuck on the air grille behind the lint screen. 7 The dryer needs a room above 7°C (45°F) to work properly.

8 If loads always come out too damp on Auto cycles, you can make all Auto cycles dry longer: with the dryer off, hold Temperature for 6 seconds, press Temperature to pick 2 (15% more) or 3 (30% more), then press START/PAUSE. 9 Steam models: if Quick Refresh leaves damp spots, finish with Enhanced Touch Up. The dryer runs but does not heat 1 Check that Air Dry is not selected.

2 Check the breakers: the drum can turn without heat if one of the two has tripped. 3 "L2" on the display means low power. Press any button to clear it and check the breakers. If it comes back, contact property management. 1 Thumping after the dryer has not been used for a while is normal and stops after a few minutes.

2 Rattling: check pockets and the front and back edges of the drum for small objects. If clothes are balled up, separate them and restart. If it still vibrates, it may not be level: contact property management. 3 Clicking on gas dryers and humming during steam cycles are normal. Wrinkles, stains, lint, smells or a hot load

1 Take clothes out as soon as the cycle ends, or use Wrinkle Shield. 2 Add dryer sheets at the start of the cycle only. Do not use them with steam cycles. 3 Hot load: let Cool Down finish before you take the load out, and use an Auto cycle with lower heat. From the manufacturer's manual, page 7. 4 Lint on clothes: clean the lint screen before each load.

5 Smell after painting nearby: air out the room, then wash and dry the clothes again. STOP AND CONTACT PROPERTY MANAGEMENT You smell gas: do not touch any switch or phone in the building. Leave, call the gas supplier from outside, then property management. A burning smell or smoke: press POWER and do not use the dryer again.

An "F" code (for example F1 E1) shows on the display, or the dryer does not heat. "AF" keeps coming back after you clean the lint screen. If you are unsure, or if the problem continues, stop using the appliance and contact property management.
Based on the manufacturer's manual W10385092A for this Whirlpool electronic dryer. Pictures are taken from that manual. Updated 20 October 2026.

TROUBLESHOOTING (— First try the solutions suggested here or visit our website at www.whirlpool.com/help \ for assistance and to possibly avoid a service call. If you experience | D Dryer will not run Possible Causes Door not closed completely. Solution Make sure the dryer door is closed completely. START/PAUSE button not pressed firmly or held long enough. Press and hold the START/PAUSE button 2-5 seconds.

Household fuse is blown or circuit breaker has tripped. There may be 2 household fuses or circuit breakers for the dryer. Check that both fuses are intact and tight, or that both circuit breakers have not tripped. Replace the fuses or reset the circuit breaker. If the problem continues, call an electrician. Incorrect power supply. Electric dryers require 240-volt power supply. Check with a qualified electrician. Wrong type of household fuse.

Use a time-delay fuse. Household fuse is blown or circuit breaker has tripped. Dryer will not heat The drum may be turning, but you may not have heat. Electric dryers use 2 household fuses or circuit breakers. Replace the fuses or reset the circuit breaker. If the problem continues, call an electrician. Incorrect power supply. Electric dryers require 240-volt power supply. Check with a qualified electrician. Supply line valve not open.

Humming or whining Water pump on dryer is running. noise with Steam cycle selected For gas dryers, make sure that the valve on the gas supply line is open The water pump on the dryer is used during the Steam function. If the dryer has just been installed or unused for an extended period, the pump may be louder and run longer. This is normal. Thumping noise Dryer hasn’t been used in a while.

This is normal. The thumping sound should diminish after a few minutes of use. A small object caught between the edges of dryer drum. Rattling or vibrating noise Check the front and rear edges of the drum for small objects. Clean out pockets before laundering. Dryer isn’t properly leveled. The dryer may vibrate if not properly installed. See the “Installation Instructions.” All four dryer feet should be in firm contact with the floor.

Clothing is balled up in dryer. When balled up, the load will bounce, causing the dryer to vibrate. Separate the load items and restart the dryer. Clicking noise Gas valve operating. Clothes are not drying satisfactorily or drying Lint screen is clogged with lint. On gas dryers, you may hear the gas valve clicking as it opens and closes. This is normal. Clean lint screen before each load.

The exhaust vent or outside exhaust hood is clogged with lint, restricting air movement. times are too long Run the dryer for 5-10 minutes. Hold your hand under the outside exhaust hood to check air movement. If you do not feel air movement, clean exhaust system of lint or replace exhaust vent with heavy metal or flexible metal vent. See “Installation Instructions.” The exhaust vent is not the correct length.

Check that the exhaust vent is not too long or has too many turns. Long venting will increase drying times. See “Installation Instructions.” The exhaust vent diameter is not the correct size. Use 4" (102 mm) diameter vent material. The dryer is not level. Clothes not contacting the moisture sensors during Automatic cycles. See “Level the Dryer” in the Installation Instructions. The Air Dry temperature setting has been selected.
Select the right temperature for the types of garments being dried. See “Cycle Guide”.

TROUBLESHOOTING (— First try the solutions suggested here or visit our website at www.whirlpool.com/help for assistance and to possibly avoid a service call. If you experience Possible Causes Solution Clothes are not drying satisfactorily or drying times are too long The load is too large and heavy to dry quickly. Separate the load to tumble freely. Dryer sheets are blocking the grille.

The air outlet grille is just inside the door, behind the lint screen. Check that it is not blocked by a dryer sheet. Use only one dryer sheet, and use it only once. The dryer is located in a room with temperature below 45°F (7°C). Proper operation of dryer cycles requires temperatures above 45°F (7°C). The dryer is located in a closet.

Closet doors must have ventilation openings at the top and bottom of the door. The front of the dryer requires a minimum of 1" (25 mm) of airspace, and, for most installations, the rear of the dryer requires 5" (127 mm). See “Installation Instructions.” Cycle time is too short The load may not be contacting the sensor strips on Auto Cycles.

Level the dryer. See “Installation Instructions.” All four dryer feet should be in firm contact with the floor. Clothes are coming out of the Quick Refresh cycle (on some models) with damp or wet spots. Under certain environmental or installation conditions you may experience underdrying. Select the Enhanced Touch Up cycle (on some models) to finish drying. The auto cycle is ending early.

Change the dryness level setting on Auto Cycles. Increasing or decreasing the dryness level will change the amount of drying time in a cycle. If loads are consistently ending too early, see also “Changing the Auto Cycle settings to increase drying time”. Lint on load Lint screen is clogged with lint. Clean lint screen before each load. Stains on load Improper use of dryer sheets.

Add dryer sheets at the beginning of the cycle. Dryer sheets added to a partially dried load can stain your garments. Do not use dryer sheets with steam cycles. Stains on drum Loose dyes in clothes. Drum stains are caused by dyes in clothing (usually blue jeans). These will not transfer to other clothing. Loads are wrinkled The load was not removed from dryer at the end of the cycle.

On steam models, select Enhanced Touch Up Cycle to tumble the load with water and heat. This cycle is best for smoothing out wrinkles and reducing odors from loads consisting of wrinkle-free cotton, cotton-polyester blends, common knits and synthetic garments. NOTE: Refer to garment care label instructions. Dry clean only garments are not recommended. The dryer was overloaded. Dry smaller loads that can tumble freely. When using the

Quick Refresh cycle (on steam models), select the correct number of garments (1-9). Results may also vary depending on fabric type. This cycle is best for reducing wrinkles and odors from loads consisting of wrinkle-free cotton, cotton- polyester blends, common knits and synthetics. Loads are wrinkled (Steam models only) Ne For steam cycles, the water is not properly connected with the dryer.
Make sure water is connected to the dryer. Check that water inlet hose is connected to both the faucet and dryer’s water inlet valve. Check that the water supply is turned on. yy, 16

If you experience Odors Possible Causes Recent painting, staining, or varnishing in the area where your dryer is located. Solution Ventilate the area. When the odors or fumes are gone from the area, rewash and dry the clothing. For steam cycles, the water is not properly connected with the dryer.

Make sure water is connected to the dryer. Check that water inlet hose is connected to both the faucet and dryer’s water inlet valve. Check that the water supply is turned on. Odors are left in garments after wearing.

To remove odors left in garments after wearing, select Quick Refresh (steam models only). This cycle is best for reducing wrinkles and odors from loads consisting of wrinkle-free cotton, cotton-polyester blends, common knits, and synthetics. Load too hot “PF” (power failure) Load removed before cooldown portion of cycle complete. Allow the dryer to complete the cooldown portion of the cycle before removing the load.

Using a cycle with a high temperature setting. The drying cycle has been interrupted by a power failure. Select an Auto Cycle with a lower heat setting to avoid overdrying the load. Press and hold START/PAUSE to restart the dryer. “L2” Diagnostic Code (low or no line voltage condition) There may be a problem with your home power supply keeping the dryer’s heater from turning on.

The dryer will continue to run when this diagnostic code is present. Press any key to clear the code from the display and return to the estimated time remaining. Try the following: Check to see if a household fuse has blown or circuit breaker has tripped. Electric dryers use two household fuses or breakers. Replace the fuse or reset the circuit breaker. Confirm the power cord is properly installed. Refer to “Installation Instructions” for details.

Select a Manual Cycle with heat, and restart the dryer. If the message persists, consult a qualified electrician. “AF” (low airflow condition) The lint screen or vent is clogged; the vent is crushed or kinked or has too many turns. The dryer will continue to run when this diagnostic code is present. Press any key to clear the code from the display and return to the estimated time remaining. Try the following: * Clean lint screen.

* Check to see if the vent run from the dryer to the wall is crushed or kinked. Confirm the vent run from the dryer to the wall is free of lint and debris. Confirm the exterior vent exhaust hood is free of lint and debris. Confirm your vent system falls within the recommended run length and number of elbows for the type of vent you are using. Refer to “Plan Vent System” in the Installaton Instructions for details.

Select a Manual Cycle with heat, and restart the dryer. If the message persists, have your entire home venting run cleaned. “F# E#” (F1 E1, F3 E1, etc.) variable service codes Ne The dryer is in need of service. If a code beginning with an “F” appears in the display. Alternating between F# and E#, the dryer control has detected a problem that requires service. Call for service. S) 17
